steps.label: jq
steps.sub: a separate tool built to query and reshape JSON itself

steps.label: --output json
steps.sub: both az and aws can emit it — jq's raw material

code:
az vm list --output json | jq -r '.[] | .name'

# .[]  -> iterate the array
# .name -> pull the name field
# -r   -> raw text, no surrounding quotes
caption: Three small pieces: iterate, extract, print raw — the building blocks of every jq filter.

eyebrow: Filtering in one pass with select()
code:
aws ec2 describe-instances --output json \
  | jq -r '.Reservations[].Instances[] \
      | select(.State.Name == "running") \
      | .InstanceId'
caption: One aws call, one jq filter — no per-instance loop needed to find just the running ones.
String interpolation with \(...) combines two fields into one readable line: web-vm-01 (eastus).
